problem: Home-screen launch after update could reject FetchEvent.respondWith with shell-network when a release redirect was not usable and no exact cached document existed.
behavior: Fetch the canonical same-origin root as a GET accepting HTML, without inheriting navigation redirect mode or following redirects.
On network failure, use a valid document from the current complete shell cache, including its canonical entry. Cache reads and fetch are bounded.
If network and shell cache are unavailable, return a real HTTP 503 document with a user-operated retry link instead of a rejected respondWith.

Cloudflare recognizes HTML navigation without Fetch Metadata so an already active legacy Safari worker can receive the current root on recognized entry URLs. Ordinary precache fetches retain immutable bytes.
No forced worker activation or reload over active music. No changes to vault, IndexedDB music, OPFS or Telegram transport.

standalone.scope: Native desktop browsers with old/new production SW bodies plus a TESTONLY version observer, local edge without Fetch Metadata, own WAV files and synthetic session vault. Includes redirects/compressed HTML, failed network, offline, purged shell cache, and retry.

limits: Linux WebKit is not physical Safari/iPhone or an installed iOS home-screen acceptance.
No real Telegram session, account, private chat, audio or profile was accessed. Session retention is tested with a synthetic vault.
No background-download job queue is implemented by this increment.

Negative attempts are preserved privately. Earlier observer waits confused transient waiting with the new install; final test waits for installed and positively identifies the active new worker. Two expected WebKit baseline browser errors are recorded only for the failing legacy page, separate from repaired-flow errors.
If the browser has independently purged its data, this change cannot restore removed authorization or music.
Public navigation acceptance was not available because preview browser reported available=false; published HTTP artifacts were verified separately. iPhone/Safari installed acceptance remains pending.
